title: K-flat resolutions and the homotopy derivability structure
statement: Let $C$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] with a monoidal structure [def-sfb-monoidal-category] whose tensor product is additive in each variable, and suppose tensoring on either side with any object preserves all small colimits. Call $M\in C$ flat if $M\otimes-$ and $-\otimes M$ are exact. Suppose there is a functor $P:C\to C$ with flat values and a natural epimorphism $P\to\operatorname{id}_C$ (a functorial flat resolution). For unbounded cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms use [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and for the direct-sum total tensor and two-sided K-flatness use [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. Then there is a functor $R:\mathrm{CoCh}(C)\to\mathrm{CoCh}(C)$ with K-flat values and a natural quasi-isomorphism $r:R\to\operatorname{id}$. Let $K(C)$ be the category with complexes as objects and cochain maps modulo cochain homotopy as morphisms: $f,g:X\to Y$ are homotopic if there are $h^n:X^n\to Y^{n-1}$ with $f^n-g^n=d_Y^{n-1}h^n+h^{n+1}d_X^n$ for every $n$. Write $W$ for its quasi-isomorphisms, and $K_{\mathrm{fl}}(C)$ for its full subcategory of K-flat objects. Its inclusion $K_{\mathrm{fl}}(C)\to K(C)$, with the restricted quasi-isomorphisms, is a left derivability structure [def-sfb-left-derivability-structure]. In particular every object of $K(C)$ admits a quasi-isomorphism from a K-flat object. No functorial choice on $K(C)$ itself is asserted.

proof.text: Shrink the Grothendieck colimits and the stipulated tensor-colimit preservation to universe zero. AB5 gives exact ordered-integer colimits. Preservation of the coproducts indexed by pairs and triples of integers supplies the graded tensor compatibility instances. The existing flat-subcategory instances in WeilConjectures.FromJoel.CategoryTheory.Abelian.Flat.KFlat then give zero, finite coproducts and idempotent completeness of the flat subcategory.

source.place: First three sentences; existing source-library colimit and flat-subcategory instances.

proof.text: Lift P to the full subcategory of flat objects using hflat. Together with p and hepi this is a LeftResolution of its inclusion. Apply the existing Mathlib LeftResolution.reduced construction, so that its cover functor preserves zero morphisms without any additivity assumption on P. Use the concrete existing LeftResolution.resolutionFunctor and resolutionNatTrans: these are the functorial bounded-above totalizations followed by the colimit of the good truncation diagram. Their quasiIso_resolutionNatTrans_app instance supplies every augmentation quasi-isomorphism. No choice of unrelated resolution witnesses is made.

Apply the existing LeftResolution.kFlat_resolutionFunctor_obj to the reduced resolution and ObjectProperty.flat.essImage_ι_le. This is precisely the bounded-above-flat K-flat theorem applied to the stages of its colimit presentation, followed by closure of K-flatness under exact integer colimits. The source monoidal K-flat predicate on complexes is definitionally IsKFlatForTotalTensor, since its two morphism actions are tensorHom (identity) s and tensorHom s (identity). This proves K-flatness of every value of the constructed resolution functor.

Identify the exact existential representative predicate in the statement with the source K-flat property on the homotopy category. Forward, a K-flat representative gives source K-flatness by HomotopyCategory.kFlat_quotient_obj_iff, and transport along its object equality. Conversely choose a complex representative using quotient_obj_surjective and apply the reverse implication of that iff. Apply LeftResolution.homotopyCategory_kFlat_isLeftDerivabilityStructure to the same reduced resolution. This is the existing homotopy-resolution criterion, with the source K-flat triangulated and isomorphism-closed instances and the same natural quasi-isomorphism. Rewrite by the proved equality of predicates. Pair this with the functor, augmentation and their properties from steps 2 and 3.
